customer-dev: Hey — seeing intermittent 500s after token refresh + deploy. Stack: RuntimeError: Event loop is closed and sometimes RuntimeError: Cannot run the event loop while another loop is running. Appears after we refresh OAuth token and recreate an httpx.AsyncClient in a background task. Using FastAPI + uvicorn --reload on Python 3.11. Versions: redwood-py 0.6.1, httpx 0.23.3, uvicorn 0.20.0. Any ideas?

customer-dev: Minimal repro below (we do lifecycle in startup and then a background coroutine re-instantiates the client on token rotate):
```py
from fastapi import FastAPI, BackgroundTasks
import asyncio
import httpx

app = FastAPI()
client = None

@app.on_event('startup')
async def startup():
    global client
    client = httpx.AsyncClient()

async def refresh_tokens_periodically():
    global client
    while True:
        await asyncio.sleep(60)
        await client.aclose()
        client = httpx.AsyncClient()  # sometimes raises RuntimeError on reload/uvicorn

@app.get('/')
async def root(background: BackgroundTasks):
    background.add_task(refresh_tokens_periodically)
    r = await client.get('https://httpbin.org/get')
    return r.json()
```

customer-dev: We also saw retries double-sending at the same time which caused duplicate billed requests — not sure if related.

ingrid: :eyes: thanks for the repro, this looks like an event-loop lifecycle bug. Can you attach the full stacktrace and confirm whether the background task runs in the same process (uvicorn reload spawns a watcher that restarts process)?

customer-dev: stack excerpt: 
```
RuntimeError: Event loop is closed
  File "uvicorn/protocols/http/h11_impl.py", line 429, in run_asgi
  File ".../asyncio/base_events.py", line 626, in run_until_complete
  RuntimeError: Cannot run the event loop while another loop is running
```
ingrid: OK — two likely causes: (1) creating/closing AsyncClient inside a task while uvicorn reloads the process can race with loop shutdown, (2) mixing sync wrappers that call asyncio.run/run_until_complete inside a running loop. Which SDK entrypoint are you using to call Redwood? are you using the sync wrapper anywhere?

customer-dev: we call redwood.sync() in a couple of legacy endpoints for convenience.

alex: that sync wrapper is probably calling asyncio.run under the hood. If asyncio.run is invoked while the server is running (FastAPI/uvicorn already has a running loop) you can get "Cannot run the event loop". Also recreating AsyncClient during shutdown can hit "Event loop is closed".

alex: Quick troubleshooting steps:
- Avoid calling sync wrappers from within request handlers in an ASGI server. Use the async client APIs instead.
- Create a single AsyncClient at app startup and rotate its auth headers instead of closing and re-instantiating on the fly.
- If you must recreate the client, do it in the app lifespan (startup/shutdown) or ensure the background task finishes before loop shutdown.
- Try upgrading httpx to 0.24.1 and redwood-py to 0.6.4; there were some fixes around AsyncClient cleanup and trio/anyio interop.

ingrid: can you also try turning off uvicorn --reload and reproduce on a plain production worker (gunicorn/uvicorn workers)? reload spawn semantics often cause confusing loop lifecycles.

rachel: quick patch we recommended to another customer: instead of closing/creating a new AsyncClient, update auth like:
```py
# keep one client
client.headers.update({'Authorization': f'Bearer {new_token}'})
```
no close/open required. Worked around the billing duplicate issue as well because we eliminated short windows where requests were retried during client recreation.

customer-dev: good call — I can try that. Any immediate mitigation if we can't change code today?

alex: short-term mitigation: pin versions to httpx==0.24.1, anyio==3.7.0, redwood-py==0.6.4 and restart. If you see the error during hot reload, disable --reload. Also audit for any redwood.sync() usage and wrap in a threadpool (run_in_executor) if you must call sync from async code.

customer-dev: thanks — I'll try the header-update approach and bump versions. Will report back.

ingrid: noted, assigning to eng-runtime to investigate broader sync-wrapper detection. tagging @alex for follow-up. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T18:10:05Z triggered by customer-dev on staging.

customer-dev: Follow-up: after switching to header update pattern and upgrading, the error stopped reproducing on staging. No more duplicate billing incidents. Thanks! :tada:
